newsitem.title: GERMANY: German authorities examine Bloomberg's TV project.
newsitem.headline: German authorities examine Bloomberg's TV project.

text.p: German media regulators said Tuesday they were weighing an application by U.S. news agency Bloomberg to start a 24-hour financial television news service in Germany.

LPR Hessen, a regional private broadcasting body for the state of Hesse, said the initial examination had gone well but a final decision on awarding a licence would rest with the newly created KEK authority, which monitors concentration of influence in various sectors.
Bloomberg, majority-owned by its founder Michael Bloomberg, wants to run the TV service from its base in Frankfurt, Hesse.

Until last January, German law banned any private company in which any party owned more than 50 percent from setting up a nationwide television information service. That restriction has since been eased.
